description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved Hong Kong bakery classic, famous for their unique crispy, crumbly topping that resembles a pineapple's skin. Beneath this sweet crust lies a soft, fluffy bread roll, creating a delightful contrast in every bite. This recipe guides you to recreate this iconic treat at home, perfect for breakfast or an afternoon snack.

ingredients.notes: 1 for bun dough, 1 for egg wash

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 250g all-purpose flour, 30g granulated sugar, 3g instant dry yeast, and 3g salt. Add 120ml lukewarm milk and 1 large egg. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for about 10 minutes, or until smooth and elastic. Gradually incorporate 25g softened unsalted butter and continue kneading until the butter is fully absorbed and the dough is very smooth and pliable. It should pass the windowpane test.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Place the kneaded dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size. This initial proofing develops the flavor and texture of the bun.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is proofing, prepare the topping. In a separate bowl, cream together 60g softened unsalted butter, 60g granulated sugar, and 20g powdered sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in 1 large egg yolk and 1/2 tsp vanilla extract (if using). Sift in 100g all-purpose flour, 10g milk powder (if using), and 1/4 tsp baking powder. Mix until just combined to form a soft, cookie-like dough. Do not overmix. Cover and chill in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns and Apply Topping
instructions.text: Once the dough has doubled, punch it down gently to release the air. Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Take the chilled pineapple topping dough and divide it into 8 equal portions. Flatten each topping portion into a thin disc, large enough to cover about two-thirds of the bun. Gently place a topping disc over each bun, pressing lightly to adhere and shape it to the bun's curvature. Use a knife to lightly score a crisscross pattern on the topping, mimicking a pineapple's skin.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Egg Wash
instructions.text: Arrange the topped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let them proof in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until noticeably puffy. Preheat your oven to 180C (350F). Just before baking, whisk the remaining egg (from the bun dough preparation) with a teaspoon of water to create an egg wash. Lightly brush the egg wash over the pineapple topping, avoiding the bun dough itself.

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Bake the pineapple buns in the preheated oven for 18-22 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crispy, and the buns are cooked through. The exact baking time may vary depending on your oven. Once baked, remove from the oven and transfer to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving. These buns are best enjoyed warm.

tips: For an even softer bun interior, ensure your dough is kneaded sufficiently until it passes the windowpane test, indicating good gluten development.
When making the pineapple topping, ensure the butter is softened but not melted. Overworking the topping dough can make it tough, so mix until just combined.
Pineapple buns are best enjoyed fresh and warm. If storing, keep them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for longer. Reheat gently in an oven or toaster oven.
article:
**The Ultimate Guide to Making Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao at Home**

There are few pastries as iconic and comforting in Chinese baking as the Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao. This beloved treat, instantly recognizable by its signature craggly, sweet crust, is a staple in Hong Kong bakeries and dim sum restaurants worldwide. Despite its name, the Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao contains no actual pineapple; its moniker comes from the golden-brown, cracked topping that resembles the fruit's rough exterior. If you’ve ever craved that perfect balance of a soft, fluffy bun and a sweet, crumbly crust, you’re in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create authentic and delicious Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao right in your own kitchen.

## What is Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao?

Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao is a classic Hong Kong sweet bun known for its unique texture contrast. The base is a soft, slightly sweet, enriched milk bread dough, similar to Japanese milk bread or a brioche. What truly sets it apart is its distinctive topping: a sweet, crumbly, cookie-like crust that bakes to a beautiful golden brown and develops a characteristic cracked pattern, reminiscent of a pineapple's skin. This topping is typically made from a mixture of sugar, flour, butter, and egg, forming a paste that is spread thinly over the unbaked bun.

Originating in Hong Kong during the 1940s, this bun quickly became a cornerstone of local bakeries and "cha chaan tengs" (Hong Kong-style cafes), where it's often enjoyed for breakfast or afternoon tea with a cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea. Its popularity has spread globally, making it a cherished pastry for many. The magic lies in that first bite – the delicate crunch of the topping yielding to the airy softness of the bun beneath. Making Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao at home allows you to enjoy them fresh from the oven, a truly unparalleled experience.

## Ingredients You Need

To make authentic Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao, you'll need two sets of ingredients: one for the soft bun dough and another for the iconic pineapple topping.

**For the Bun Dough:**
*   **All-Purpose Flour:** 3 cups (about 360g) – provides structure.
*   **Granulated Sugar:** 1/4 cup (about 50g) – sweetness and helps activate yeast.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 2 teaspoons – for leavening.
*   **Salt:** 1/2 teaspoon – enhances flavor.
*   **Warm Milk:** 3/4 cup (about 180ml), around 105-115°F (40-46°C) – activates yeast, adds moisture and richness.
*   **Large Egg:** 1, at room temperature – adds richness, color, and helps bind.
*   **Unsalted Butter:** 1/4 cup (4 tablespoons or 56g), softened – for tenderness and flavor.

**For the Pineapple Topping:**
*   **All-Purpose Flour:** 1 cup (about 120g) – main structure of the topping.
*   **Powdered Sugar (Confectioners' Sugar):** 1/2 cup (about 60g) – for sweetness and fine texture.
*   **Milk Powder:** 2 tablespoons (optional, but highly recommended for richer flavor).
*   **Baking Powder:** 1/2 teaspoon (optional, for a lighter, crispier topping).
*   **Unsalted Butter:** 1/2 cup (1 stick or 113g), softened – for richness and crumbly texture.
*   **Large Egg Yolk:** 1, at room temperature – for binding and color.
*   **Vanilla Extract:** 1/2 teaspoon (optional, for enhanced flavor).

**For Egg Wash (optional, for shine):**
*   **Large Egg:** 1, beaten with 1 tablespoon water.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao involves several stages, but each step is straightforward. Patience is key!

**1. Prepare the Bun Dough:**
    *   In a large bowl, combine warm milk, 1 teaspoon of sugar, and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
    *   In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, remaining sugar, and salt.
    *   Add the egg and yeast mixture to the dry ingredients. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
    *   Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface or into a stand mixer with a dough hook. Knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
    *   Gradually incorporate the softened butter, kneading until fully absorbed and the dough is soft, smooth, and passes the windowpane test (a small piece of dough can be stretched thin enough to see light through it without tearing).
    *   Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it proof in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

**2. Prepare the Pineapple Topping:**
    *   In a medium bowl, cream together the softened butter and powdered sugar until light and fluffy.
    *   Beat in the egg yolk and vanilla extract (if using) until well combined.
    *   In a separate small bowl, whisk together the flour, milk powder (if using), and baking powder (if using).
    *   Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined and a soft, pliable dough forms. Do not overmix.
    *   Divide the topping dough into 12 equal portions. Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. This makes it easier to handle.

**3. Shape the Buns and Apply Topping:**
    *   Once the bun dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release air.
    *   Divide the dough into 12 equal portions (about 50-60g each).
    *   Shape each portion into a smooth ball. Place them on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, leaving space between each.
    *   Take one portion of chilled topping dough. Flatten it between two pieces of plastic wrap or parchment paper into a thin circle, slightly larger than the bun.
    *   Carefully peel off the top plastic wrap and invert the topping circle onto a bun. Gently press and smooth it over the top of the bun, letting it drape slightly down the sides.
    *   Repeat for all buns. If desired, use a sharp knife to gently score a crosshatch pattern on the topping (don't cut too deep into the bun).
    *   Cover the buns loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let them proof again in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy (they won't quite double this time).

**4. Bake the Pineapple Buns:**
    *   Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
    *   If using, gently brush the egg wash over the exposed bun dough (not the topping).
    *   Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the buns are cooked through.
    *   Remove from the oven and let cool slightly on a wire rack.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Don't Rush Proofing:** Allow the dough ample time to rise in a warm, draft-free environment. Proper proofing is essential for soft, fluffy buns. Under-proofed buns will be dense, while over-proofed ones can collapse.
*   **Hydration is Key:** The bun dough should be soft and slightly sticky after kneading. Avoid adding too much extra flour, as this can lead to dry buns.
*   **Chill the Topping:** Chilling the pineapple topping dough makes it much easier to handle and roll out without it sticking to your hands or the rolling pin.
*   **Even Topping Application:** Aim for an even thickness when rolling out the topping. This ensures it bakes uniformly and develops that beautiful, consistent crackle.
*   **Scoring:** Scoring the topping before baking is optional but gives the Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao its classic look. Use a very sharp knife and score gently, only through the topping layer.
*   **Eat Them Fresh:** Pineapple buns are best enjoyed warm, fresh from the oven, when the topping is at its crispiest and the bun is at its softest.

## Serving Suggestions

Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao is incredibly versatile in how it can be enjoyed. The most classic way is simply on its own, perhaps with a cup of hot coffee or traditional Hong Kong milk tea.

For an extra decadent experience, try the "Bo Lo Yau" version: slice the warm bun horizontally and insert a thick slab of cold, unsalted butter into the middle. The contrasting temperatures and textures of the warm bun, crisp topping, and melting butter are simply divine. It's a rich treat that's hard to beat!

They also make a fantastic breakfast item or a satisfying afternoon snack. Some people even enjoy them with a slice of cheese or a fried egg inside, though this is less traditional.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao is perfect as is, there are many ways to get creative:

*   **Fillings:** Elevate your buns by adding a filling! Popular choices include red bean paste, custard cream, shredded coconut, or even savory char siu (BBQ pork) for a delightful sweet and savory contrast. Simply flatten the dough ball, place a tablespoon of filling in the center, and pinch the dough closed before shaping it back into a ball.
*   **Topping Flavors:** Experiment with the topping by adding a teaspoon of matcha powder for a green tea flavor, or cocoa powder for a chocolate pineapple bun.
*   **Vegan Options:** With the increasing availability of plant-based ingredients, you can make a vegan version. Use plant-based milk, vegan butter, and substitute the egg in the bun dough with a flax egg (1 tablespoon ground flaxseed + 3 tablespoons water) or an egg replacer. For the topping, use vegan butter and omit the egg yolk.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While challenging due to the importance of gluten in bread structure, gluten-free all-purpose flour blends can be used, though the texture of the bun may differ. Look for blends designed for bread baking.

Mastering the art of making Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao at home is a rewarding culinary journey. The aroma of freshly baked buns filling your kitchen is an experience in itself, and the taste of your homemade creation will transport you straight to the bustling bakeries of Hong Kong. Enjoy the process, and savor every delicious bite!
